memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium. Adecco (ADEN-CH) is a cyclical recovery case with self-help inside a leveraged, low-quality business, bought after its first part: at CHF 23.84 (2026-10-09) the 'Modal return' is 8.4 percent a year over eighteen months and 10.9 percent a year over three years against the 20 percent bar, a D. The park rule applies because 'Business' (E 2, BB 2) is D and the record does not argue otherwise: the D is the reason the modal return is not reached (dilution, leverage, mix), not a flaw in how the case is argued; management is C, predictability C, trackability B, so the gate closes on one of its four conditions. Not bearish, because the yield is covered, the cycle is turning, the cost base is real and the research's "false friend" is plausible rather than probable. The case re-opens either at a price in the clearing range (EUR 20 to 22 on the FactSet quote; CHF 18.8 to 20.5 by the same percentages, where the shares traded in June and July 2026) or on Q3 2026 results (2026-11-12) showing gross margin at or above 18.8 percent with FY2026 leverage guided below 2.5x and the Belgian temporary-staffing series no worse than -3 percent, which together would move the gross margin and leverage conditions to probable and the 'Modal return' toward C. Pattern: 'Trough on Trough', fit C, caught six months late; secondary 'Major Corporate Change', fit C.
case: The change is external and cyclical and it has arrived at the company. European temporary-staffing demand fell for about two years (organic -5.0 percent in Q3 2024; -2 percent FY2024; +1 percent FY2025) and has turned: five consecutive quarters of organic growth, +5.3 percent in Q1 2026 and +5.6 percent in Q2 2026, against Randstad's +1.9 percent and ManpowerGroup's +6.0 percent constant currency; broad across regions (Americas +12 percent; North American SME +23 percent; APAC +10 percent; Iberia +22 percent; France -1 percent). The visibility is two quarters, not two years: Belgian temp hours -7.6 percent year on year in August 2026 from -4.4 percent in July; ING's series -5.1 percent; Eurozone GDP forecast 0.9 percent for 2026; comparables harden by about 300 basis points from Q3 2026; management guides to year-on-year growth slowing. So the own-cycle Key Question is B, demand C, macro D (a force acting on Adecco more than the universe through the 40 percent European industrial exposure and France), external forces C.

The internal change is mostly delivered, which is why the volume drops through. G&A savings EUR 174 million against EUR 150 million (nearly EUR 200 million against 2022), SG&A 3.2 percent of revenue, DSO 53 days, Akkodis Germany utilisation 91 percent, perimeter pruned in small steps (Entegee sold June 2026; Akkodis Germany non-core units sold; General Assembly B2C exited; Pontoon moved into Adecco), strategy re-set at the November 2025 Capital Markets Day (RUN and CHANGE; AI-first; Akkodis pivot to aerospace and defence toward 20 to 25 percent of its revenue by 2030; offshore), the AI deployment ahead of plan (50 percent agent-enabled revenue reached a quarter early; 70 percent target). Result: Q2 2026 EBITA +21 percent organic on +5.6 percent revenue, 64 percent drop-through, adjusted EPS +31 percent. What is not there: no new chief executive (fifth year; Sodexo record of revenue EUR 20,698 million to EUR 17,428 million and margin 6.5 to 3.3 percent, mandate ended 2021), no raised financial guidance (3 to 6 percent corridor, 3 percent floor; growth targets withdrawn, shares -11 percent on the day), a balance sheet being de-utilised (2.7x against 1.5x; buybacks halted since early 2022; hybrid EUR 450 million at 4.875 percent) and shareholder returns cut (dividend -60 percent; scrip 53.01 percent). The screen's rule of three strong forces is not met: two strong, one moderate, three running the wrong way. Internal forces C; 'Change Forces' C.

'Financial Outputs' have turned up on three of four lines and the fourth is the business model. Revenue growth from -3.4 percent (FY2024) to +3.8 percent reported in Q2 2026 (B); EBITA margin from the 3.0 percent floor to +30 basis points year on year with consensus EBITDA margin 3.7 to 4.1 percent by FY2028 (B); net debt to EBITDA 3.2x to 2.7x in a year (B); cash conversion 83 percent trailing after 102 percent, H1 2026 free cash flow negative on growth working capital (D). Key metrics B under the framework's conditional rule: near-term outputs very positive on the margin and EPS lines, and the 64 percent drop-through on a cost base that no longer grows is the plausible logic for continuation. But the gross margin, the line the cost programme cannot reach, fell 30 basis points year on year to 18.6 percent on enterprise mix (-60 in Q1), guided to about 18.8 percent in Q3; the research's change-of-mind trigger is two quarters above 19.0 percent with EBITA above 3.2 percent. Sell-side upgrades possible, not probable (C): the 22 percent EPS beat moved targets +18 percent and estimates +0.5 percent over three months; dashboard revisions D (EPS -1, 0, -8 percent over one, three, six months); skew about even over three months, clearly negative over six and twelve; guidance in line with consensus, not above; no house argues guidance is conservative; the chief executive's record is an honest tracker on costs, not an upgrader. Goldilocks growth C: mid-teens over six months (B), about 8 percent over eighteen months (C; EUR 2.46 to EUR 2.66, consensus EUR 2.71), 11 to 12 percent a year over three years from the FY2025 adjusted base (C), once 1.5 to 2 percent a year of scrip dilution is counted. Staircase C: dated steps (Q3 results 2026-11-12; Agentforce rollout to 40 countries; 70 percent AI target; Axiscades and Sogéclair closings; German fixed-term reform January 2027; FY2026 results and dividend proposal February 2027; April 2027 AGM; H1 2027 leverage against 2.2x; end-2027 1.5x target and the end of the scrip), all known to the sell-side and the company.
counter_case: The bull's case, at full force. Adecco is the first European generalist staffer back in organic growth, five quarters running and 370 basis points ahead of Randstad (+5.6 against +1.9 percent). It trades at 8.6x earnings that themselves sit at a ten-year margin low, the 29th percentile of its own ten-year range and a 23 percent discount to Randstad's 11.2x; Bernstein values it at 1.6x to 1.7x EV to net fees, "near historic trough levels". It yields 4.2 percent, covered 52 percent of Viewforth-definition EPS and about twice by free cash flow in a normal year. It has removed about EUR 200 million of cost that does not return when volume does, and the 64 percent drop-through of Q2 2026 shows what that cost base does; it has deployed agentic AI across half its revenue on a fixed-cost licence faster than any product in its history. It is deleveraging at about 0.5x a year (3.2x to 2.7x) with consensus debt falling from EUR 3,034 million to EUR 2,214 million by FY2028. The sell-side is still 46 percent Hold-or-worse with estimates flat after a 22 percent beat, so the upgrade cycle has not started; momentum is pinned D only because the 200-day average has been rising for less than half a year; the Belgian series is one small country in one month. All of that is what "before the crowd" looks like, and the eleven attributes at D or F are the trough's signature, not the case's flaw: a D on robustness here is a D on every trough-on-trough turn ever bought at the right time. On this reading consensus earnings are delivered without dilution (the scrip ends in 2027 as leverage passes 2x) and the multiple goes to Randstad's 11x within eighteen months: EUR 3.38 of 24-month-forward earnings at 11x plus EUR 1.07 is EUR 38.3, a 51 percent return, 32 percent a year, an A. Bernstein's "Into the up-cycle" and Deutsche Bank's "Recovery broadens, value remains" are the research's versions. A second counter-case at Building Block 2: scale plus compliance plus a single AI-enabled platform is a moat in the making, and the 160 basis points of share gain in Q2 2026, the fourteenth quarter of outgrowth in sixteen, is its first evidence; enterprise mix is the price of locking in the top 40 accounts and the AI layer then takes out the cost of serving them. A third at Building Block 3: the strict reading that two failed mandatories make the fit D and the case should wait for the bottom quartile; or the opposite, that the growth is the cost programme and AI showing through, so 'Major Corporate Change' is primary and the fit is B.

The record's concessions, in full: the cost base is real and the drop-through is real; the valuation is low against the long history and against the one true peer; the sell-side has not yet moved its estimates; if leverage reaches 2.2x by mid-2027 the fair multiple is the ten-year median of 9.5x, the record's 8.9x blend is too low by about 7 percent, and the eighteen-month return is 13.0 percent a year, a C, the conceded floor; the environment's readings and the red-flag count are partly the trough's signature; compliance load does favour scale, MSP retention is above 100 percent, the single Salesforce instance is a real asset, the share gain is real; the two failed conditions are the ones that make the pattern pay, and the price at which the fit becomes crisp again is knowable and stated.
triggers: - Re-open the case: price in the clearing range, EUR 20 to 22 on the FactSet quote (CHF 18.8 to 20.5 by the same percentages); or Q3 2026 (2026-11-12) gross margin at or above 18.8 percent with FY2026 leverage guided below 2.5x and the Belgian series no worse than -3 percent together.

- What would make the gross margin inflection probable: two consecutive quarters above 19.0 percent with EBITA above 3.2 percent (the research's trigger); unlikely: two quarters below 18.5 percent, which takes the margin component out of the path. Alarm: Q3 2026 below 18.7 percent.
- Volume cycle: Alarm Q3 2026 organic growth below +3 percent; Invalidate two quarters at or below zero; a Q3 revenue miss makes the top-line red flag present.

- European softness: Alarm a second month of Belgian hours below -5 percent; Invalidate three months below -5 percent with company organic growth below +2 percent; the bear case is invalidated by European manufacturing PMIs above 55.

- Deleveraging: 2.2x by H1 2027 at even odds; 1.5x by end-2027 unlikely (about one in three); FY2026 leverage below 2.5x with free cash flow above EUR 350 million would move 2.2x to probable and 1.5x to plausible. Alarm above 2.5x at FY2026; Invalidate leverage rising year on year at any half-year; a downgrade at either agency is an Alarm, BBB- or Baa3 an Invalidate.

- AI cost to serve: gross profit per recruiter up 5 percent or more with the SG&A ratio at or below 3.1 percent would change the view; Invalidate gross profit per recruiter flat for two quarters with agent coverage above 70 percent; Alarm SG&A above 3.3 percent with volume growing.
